rv.q: In Lu Kemp's precisely paced production, O'Connor reads Ossian's text aloud and hears it sung back to him in Gaelic, its supposed language of origin.
An entertaining historical examination of Scotland’s public image

O’Connor tackles his theme through the tale of Scottish poet James Macpherson, who back in 1760 produced a wildly popular book of epic poetry which he claimed was translated the work of a 3rd century Gaelic bard, Ossian.
Through the Shortbread Tin is thought-provoking, constantly pulling the rug from under you, making you reexamine your relationship to both your own story and that of Scotland.

cn.t: Critics praise this witty, provocative examination of Scotland's infamous Ossian hoax, finding it an intricate exploration of national identity and literary deception that casts the 18th-century fraud in fresh, compelling light.
